title: Conduction System Pacing in Pediatric Patients: Outcomes From a Multicenter International Cohort.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) may be advantageous in children requiring lifelong ventricular pacing, but long-term durability data are limited. OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate the long-term preservation, durability, and safety of CSP in pediatric patients. METHODS: This international, multicenter, retrospective study included consecutive patients aged ≤18 years undergoing His bundle pacing or left bundle branch area pacing at 9 experienced centers. The primary endpoint was long-term preservation of CSP. RESULTS: Among 120 patients (mean age 12.6 ± 3.7 years), 68 (56.7%) had congenital atrioventricular block, 41 (34.2%) had congenital heart disease, and 12 (10.0%) underwent CSP for heart failure/cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). Acute CSP implantation, defined as achievement of His bundle pacing, left bundle branch pacing, or left ventricular septal pacing, was successful in 116 patients (96.7%). After a median follow-up of 24 months (Q1-Q3: 10-54 months), electrical lead performance remained stable. Among 101 patients with CSP at implantation and follow-up capture assessment, CSP was preserved in 95 (94.1%). Kaplan-Meier-estimated freedom from loss of CSP was 100.0% at 1 year and 98.2% (95% CI: 94.7%-100.0%) at 2 and 3 years. CSP lead-related complications occurred in 10 patients (8.3%), and reintervention was required in 9 (7.5%). In the CRT subgroup, left ventricular ejection fraction improved from 28.8% ± 9.4% to 46.8% ± 12.0% (P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: CSP is a feasible, safe, and durable physiological pacing strategy in children, with excellent long-term CSP preservation and stable electrical performance despite ongoing somatic growth. CSP may also provide effective physiological resynchronization in pediatric patients requiring CRT.

title: Beyond anticoagulation: defining the role of left atrial appendage closure in stroke prevention for atrial fibrillation.
abstract: Oral anticoagulation has a very strong evidence base for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) at elevated thromboembolic risk. Direct oral anticoagulants have improved the safety and convenience of treatment, yet important limitations remain, including residual ischaemic stroke, major bleeding, treatment discontinuation, and patient refusal. Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) offers an alternative strategy for selected patients by excluding the principal anatomical source of AF-related cardiac thrombi. However, the appropriate role of LAAC remains controversial, particularly in patients who can and do tolerate anticoagulation. This viewpoint argues for a more individualized approach that distinguishes absolute contraindications from modifiable bleeding risks, treatment refusal or non-persistence, and stroke occurring despite adequate anticoagulation.

title: Mapping and Outcome Implications of Left Atrial Low Voltage Regions as Determined by a Novel 122-electrode Spherical Mapping and Ablation Catheter.
abstract: AIMS: A novel 122-electrode spherical mapping/pulsed field ablation (PFA) device is known to effectively ablate atrial fibrillation (AF). The aim of this study is threshold optimization of LVA for the unique geometry of the Globe electrodes and the prognostic association, to evaluate if the extent of low voltage areas could predict recurrence. METHODS AND RESULTS: The PULSAR study was an IDE trial of 183 patients undergoing first-time paroxysmal AF ablation with one-year outcomes of any atrial arrhythmia. During this study, a subset of patients (n=82) had detailed pre-ablation voltage maps performed with the catheter. Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) was then performed with PFA. Patients were followed with weekly transtelephonic monitoring, ECG, and Holters at 3, 6, and 12 months. Recurrence was defined as any atrial arrhythmia (AA) > 30 seconds.Receiver operator curve (ROC) analysis revealed that a low voltage threshold of 1.0 mV had the highest value (0.735). The percentage LVA surface area resulting from a threshold of 1.0 mV that predicted AA recurrence was 11.6%. Univariate and multivariate analysis revealed the percentage LVA was the strongest predictor of AA recurrence. The 12-month freedom from AA was 84.6% and 52.9% for subjects under and over the low voltage area threshold respectively. CONCLUSIONS: A voltage threshold of 1.0 mV is proposed as a threshold for defining LVA using the spherical catheter, but a range of approximately 0.5-1.5 mV yielded similar performance. Increased low voltage area in the pre-ablation atrial map was associated with a higher risk of AA recurrence.

title: Multivessel Assessment by Angiography-Derived Index of Microcirculatory Resistance in Patients With Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Current guidelines recommend testing for coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) in the left anterior descending coronary artery, and it is unclear whether multivessel assessment can improve the diagnostic yield and prognostic value of CMD. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic implications of multivessel CMD assessment using angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance (angio-IMR) in patients with nonobstructive coronary artery disease (NOCAD). METHODS: Angio-IMR was measured in all 3 major coronary arteries in 439 patients with NOCAD. Single-vessel assessment was defined as angio-IMR measurement in the left anterior descending coronary artery only. Multivessel assessment was defined as angio-IMR measurement in all 3 major coronary arteries. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events, comprising a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and hospitalization for heart failure. RESULTS: Multivessel assessment identified more patients with CMD than single-vessel assessment (46.7% vs 24.1%; P < 0.001). During a median follow-up period of 4.3 years, an increased number of vessels with CMD was associated with a higher risk for major adverse cardiovascular events after adjustment for diabetes mellitus, smoking, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and history of myocardial infarction (adjusted HR: 1.963 per vessel; 95% CI: 1.513-2.548; P < 0.001). Multivessel assessment showed superior prognostic performance compared with single-vessel assessment when added to a clinical risk factor model (area under the curve: 0.751 vs 0.707; P = 0.034). CONCLUSIONS: Multivessel assessment by angio-IMR improved the diagnostic yield of CMD and added incremental prognostic information compared with single-vessel assessment in patients with NOCAD.

title: Prevalence of Angiographic Coronary Artery Disease in Systolic Heart Failure Without Infarct-Pattern Late Gadolinium Enhancement: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: AIMS: Rest late gadolinium enhancement cardiovascular magnetic resonance (LGE-CMR) identifies infarct-pattern scar but does not assess coronary anatomy. We estimated the prevalence of angiographic coronary artery disease (CAD) among adults with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) or otherwise unexplained left ventricular systolic dysfunction without infarct-pattern LGE. METHODS AND RESULTS: MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched to 27 July 2026. Eligible studies provided separable scar-negative denominators and corresponding angiographic CAD counts from invasive coronary angiography (ICA). Scar-negative was defined as the absence of subendocardial or transmural LGE in a coronary distribution. Random-effects logit meta-analysis used restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. Twenty-two reports representing 20 studies included 2,236 paired LGE-CMR and ICA. 818 patients had infarct-pattern scar, and 1,418 were scar-negative. Eight studies contributed 44 CAD cases among 468 scar-negative patients for ≥50% stenosis, giving a pooled prevalence of 10.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] 7.4-15.4). Five studies contributed 19 CAD cases among 271 scar-negative patients for ≥70% stenosis, giving a pooled prevalence of 7.6% (95% CI 4.4-12.6). Seven studies contributed 33 CAD cases among 679 scar-negative patients for high-risk-pattern CAD, giving a pooled prevalence of 4.9% (95% CI 2.2-10.6) and a 95% prediction interval of 0.8-24.8%. These strata represented different study subsets and were not nested. CONCLUSION: Among selected adults with HFrEF or otherwise unexplained LVSD who underwent paired LGE-CMR and ICA, absence of infarct-pattern LGE did not exclude angiographic CAD. Further coronary assessment should be considered when resolving that uncertainty would alter diagnosis or management.

title: Cerebral Blood Flow-Derived Myogenic Dynamics Reveal Impaired Postischemic Cerebrovascular Recovery in Experimental Stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Restoration of cerebral blood flow (CBF) after ischemic stroke does not necessarily indicate recovery of cerebrovascular regulation. We tested whether myogenic-band dynamics derived directly from CBF signals provide information beyond mean perfusion during cerebral ischemia and after acute stroke. METHODS: Transient focal cerebral ischemia was induced in 29 Sprague-Dawley rats using middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion. Bilateral laser-Doppler flowmetry (LDF)-derived CBF signals were decomposed using empirical mode decomposition and Hilbert transform, and myogenic-band activity (0.15-0.4 Hz) was quantified by absolute and relative power. Cross-validated logistic regression models were used to evaluate whether myogenic-band power provided discriminative information beyond mean CBF alone. RESULTS: Ipsilateral mean CBF fell from 73.5±51.8 p.u. at baseline to 52.2±38.0 p.u. during late ischemia (P=0.0088), then increased to 126.6±91.5 p.u. after 3 hours of reperfusion (P=0.0050 versus baseline). Relative myogenic-band power decreased from 37.43±14.65% to 13.35±7.51% during ischemia (P<0.0001) and remained below baseline after reperfusion (20.74±12.02%, P=0.00033 versus baseline); contralateral relative power was comparatively preserved. Combining mean CBF and myogenic-band power improved discrimination of baseline from late ischemia (AUC, 0.99 versus 0.70 for mean CBF alone) and late reperfusion (AUC, 0.88 versus 0.70). CONCLUSIONS: Frequency-specific analysis of LDF-derived CBF reveals persistent, lateralized abnormalities in myogenic-band dynamics that are not captured by mean perfusion alone. The persistence of depressed myogenic activity despite restored or elevated mean CBF demonstrates incomplete recovery of frequency-specific oscillatory dynamics after reperfusion. These findings support myogenic-band power as a potential functional measure of persistent postischemic cerebrovascular dysfunction.

title: Implementation of Single-Pill Combination Therapy Through Team-Based Care for Hypertension Control in Resource-Constrained Settings: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Single-pill combination therapy improves medication adherence and hypertension control. However, limited evidence is available on its implementation in routine clinical practice. OBJECTIVE: To assess the long-term effectiveness, implementation, and sustainability of single-pill combination therapy through team-based care for blood pressure reduction among patients with uncontrolled hypertension in primary care settings in Colombia and Jamaica. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Multicountry, unblinded, pragmatic, cluster randomized clinical trial. Twenty primary care clinics in Jamaica and 20 in Colombia were randomly assigned to either the single-pill combination therapy group or the standard care group. A total of 1706 adults with uncontrolled hypertension were enrolled between February 23, 2023, and September 12, 2024. The final follow-up visit occurred on September 9, 2026. INTERVENTIONS: In the intervention group (n = 869), a team-based care approach that included physician and nurse training, health coaching, home blood pressure monitoring, and blood pressure audit and feedback was used to implement single-pill combination therapy. Single-pill combinations were purchased locally and provided to patients. In the standard care group (n = 837), patients received monotherapy or polytherapy with guideline-recommended medications covered by health insurance or government programs. The intervention lasted 18 months, with additional follow-up at 24 months. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in systolic blood pressure from baseline to 18 months. Three blood pressure measurements were obtained at each of 2 visits at each time point using a standard protocol. RESULTS: Among the 1706 enrolled participants, at baseline, the mean age was 61.4 years, 69.9% of participants were female, and 98.2% were taking antihypertensive medications. Among the 1574 participants included in the primary analysis, systolic blood pressure decreased by 19.1 mm Hg, from 145.9 mm Hg at baseline to 126.8 mm Hg at 18 months, in the intervention group and by 9.0 mm Hg, from 145.0 mm Hg to 136.1 mm Hg, in the standard care group, with a between-group difference of -10.1 mm Hg (95% CI, -13.3 to -6.9 mm Hg; P < .001). At 18 months, 69.5% of patients in the intervention group and 29.2% in the standard care group achieved systolic blood pressure less than 130 and diastolic blood pressure less than 80 mm Hg. Serious adverse events (death and hospitalization) occurred at similar frequencies in the intervention (7.9%) and standard care (9.9%) groups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Implementing single-pill combination therapy through team-based care significantly reduced blood pressure over 18 months among adults with uncontrolled hypertension in Colombia and Jamaica. This comprehensive strategy integrating single-pill combination therapy with team-based care could be widely adopted and scaled up for hypertension control, particularly in resource-constrained settings. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05405920.

title: Guided P2Y12 inhibitor selection after rapid CYP2C19 genotyping in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Dual antiplatelet therapy remains the standard treatment following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). While prasugrel and ticagrelor offer consistent antiplatelet effects, they increase bleeding risk compared with clopidogrel, which requires CYP2C19 bioactivation. AIMS: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of rapid CYP2C19 genotyping at the time of PCI on P2Y12 inhibitor selection and clinical outcomes in real-world patients. METHODS: A total of 974 patients who underwent PCI and rapid CYP2C19 genotyping and received P2Y12 inhibitor treatment were included. P2Y12 inhibitor selection, P2Y12 inhibitor switching, major atherothrombotic events (MAE; a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, stent thrombosis, or unstable angina requiring revascularisation), and bleeding events were assessed throughout the first year post-PCI. Time-varying Cox regression analysis was performed to assess event risk in patients treated with clopidogrel (reference) versus prasugrel/ticagrelor after stratifying by loss-of-function (LOF) status and adjusting for stratum-specific confounders. RESULTS: Clopidogrel was prescribed more frequently at discharge among CYP2C19 non-LOF versus LOF carriers (43% [296/691] vs 31% [87/283]; p<0.001). The median duration of follow-up was 359 days (interquartile range [IQR] 190-362 days). Among LOF allele carriers de-escalating to clopidogrel, the median de-escalation time was 180 days (IQR 92-354 days). MAE were not significantly different between P2Y12 inhibitor regimens after stratifying by LOF status (LOF-prasugrel/ticagrelor [n=147] vs LOF-clopidogrel [n=136]: adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.87 [95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.36-2.10]; non-LOF-prasugrel/ticagrelor [n=272] vs non-LOF-clopidogrel [n=419]: adjusted HR 1.26, 95% CI: 0.67-2.36). No significant differences in Bleeding Academic Research Consortium bleeding events were observed. CONCLUSIONS: This real-world study shows that, among LOF carriers managed with rapid CYP2C19 genotyping and delayed de-escalation, ischaemic and bleeding event rates were not significantly different between those taking clopidogrel versus those taking prasugrel/ticagrelor, though findings should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in transcatheter mitral interventions: percutaneous anterior leaflet modification.
abstract: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) remains one of the most catastrophic complications of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) interventions, including TMVR in native valve, valve-in-valve, valve-in-ring, and valve-in-mitral annular calcification procedures. Its incidence varies widely across procedural types (0%-40%), with mortality rates approaching 36%, and represents a leading cause of patient ineligibility, excluding 4%-50% of candidates from TMVR. Accurate pre-procedural risk stratification relies on cardiac computed tomography, which enables annular sizing, virtual valve implantation, neo- and skirt neo-left ventricular outflow tract area quantification, and fluoroscopic projection planning. Key anatomic determinants of LVOTO include anterior mitral leaflet length, aortomitral angle, septal hypertrophy, left ventricular cavity size, and device-related factors. To mitigate LVOTO risk and expand treatment eligibility, in addition to septal modification, anterior mitral leaflet modification techniques have emerged, broadly categorized into electrosurgical laceration approaches-LAMPOON and ELASTA-and balloon-assisted translocation techniques for balloon-expandable valves-BATMAN, CLEVE, DETROIT, and ROBIN. Each strategy addresses distinct anatomic substrates and procedural scenarios, and their complementary profiles support individualized technique selection. This review aims to present an in-depth discussion of LVOTO in TMVR and anterior leaflet modification strategies.

title: Impact of Infarct Type on Serious Arrhythmic Event Detection and Cardiovascular Outcomes During Telemedical Monitoring After Myocardial Infarction: A SMART-MI substudy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with LVEF 36-50% and cardiac autonomic dysfunction remain at risk after myocardial infarction (MI) despite not qualifying for primary-preventive defibrillator therapy. Implantable cardiac monitor (ICM)-based telemonitoring facilitates early detection of serious arrhythmic events (SArE), however it remains unclear whether infarct type modifies the detection and prognostic significance of SArE. OBJECTIVE: To compare the effect of ICM monitoring on SArE detection by infarct type and explore associations with subsequent major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE). METHODS: SMART-MI randomized MI survivors with LVEF 36-50% and cardiac autonomic dysfunction to ICM-based telemonitoring or conventional follow-up. Cox models assessed effects on SArE detection and treatment-by-infarct-type interaction. Exploratory analyses modeled detected SArE as a time-dependent covariate, stratified by arm, for subsequent MACCE. RESULTS: 400 patients were randomized to ICM implantation (n=201, 122 STEMI) or conventional follow-up (n=199, 114 STEMI). Telemedical monitoring increased SArE detection in STEMI (HR 11.99, 95% CI 3.67-39.17) and NSTEMI (HR 4.44, 95% CI 2.09-9.43; both p<0.001). Although the effect was numerically greater in STEMI, clinically relevant effect modification cannot be excluded (p for interaction=0.154). Detected SArE were associated with subsequent MACCE in both, STEMI and NSTEMI with HR of 7.77 (95% CI 3.20-18.86) and 4.26 (95% CI 1.44-12.58), respectively. CONCLUSION: ICM-based telemonitoring increased SArE detection in both STEMI and NSTEMI patients and detected SArE were associated with subsequent MACCE in both infarct types. These findings support further investigation of intensified rhythm-surveillance strategies in high-risk STEMI and NSTEMI patients.

title: Multiomics Integration Reveals a Skeletal Muscle Metabolic Myopathy in Cardiometabolic HFpEF.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Skeletal muscle dysfunction is a major peripheral determinant of exercise intolerance and physical disability in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Metabolic and mitochondrial dysfunction are considered to be key components of skeletal muscle dysfunction, but comprehensive profiling of metabolic pathways has not been conducted. Elucidation of dysregulated metabolic pathways is essential to determine viable targets for the treatment of exercise intolerance in HFpEF. METHODS: Male ZSF1 Obese rats (HFpEF, n=8) and Wistar Kyoto lean normotensive controls (Control, n=8) were studied at 26 weeks of age. The gastrocnemius was analyzed using bulk RNA sequencing, proteomics, metabolomics, and lipidomics. Differential expression across all omics layers was determined using standard statistical modeling with thresholds of absolute fold‑change >1.5 and FDR <0.05, unless otherwise specified. Additional targeted plasma and skeletal muscle metabolomics and lipidomics were performed in HFpEF and control rats, including analyses of the soleus and the extensor digitorum longus, to validate features associated with predominantly oxidative and glycolytic muscle, respectively. RESULTS: Pathway-level analysis for RNA sequencing and proteomics revealed significant downregulation of oxidative phosphorylation (natural enrichment score (NES), -2.1; P<0.005), electron transport chain (NES, -2.0; P<0.005), and tricarboxylic acid cycle cycle (-1.8; P<0.05). The most upregulated pathways were PPAR signaling (NES, 2.2; P<0.0001), tryptophan metabolism (NES, 1.8; P<0.005), and amino acid oxidation (NES, 1.8; P<0.005) pathways. Metabolomics revealed an accumulation of tricarboxylic acid cycle cycle intermediate, isocitrate, and phosphate reduction. Branched-chain amino acids were significantly increased, whereas amino acids related to tryptophan metabolism were reduced and shifted towards increased serotonin accumulation. Phospholipid species were differentially regulated with increased palmitoylated phosphatidylcholines but reduced arachidonoyl-phosphatidylcholine species. Phosphatidylethanolamines species (16:0/16:1-18:0/18:2) were increased. CONCLUSIONS: HFpEF skeletal muscle shows signatures of profound mitochondrial and peroxisomal dysfunction with lipid overload, impaired branched chain amino acid and tryptophan metabolism, and a shift in membrane phospholipid composition, supporting an acquired metabolic myopathy in cardiometabolic HFpEF.

title: Initial Diabetes Therapy After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting and Long-Term Outcomes.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is common among patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), but optimal post-CABG glucose-lowering therapy remains uncertain. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the OptumLabs Data Warehouse of adults with T2D undergoing isolated CABG from 2012-2024. Follow-up began 30 days after discharge. Glucose-lowering therapy was modeled as a time-varying exposure with patients contributing no-observed-therapy person-time until the first qualifying post-discharge fill. Pairwise comparisons used stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were heart failure hospitalization, stroke, and repeat coronary revascularization. RESULTS: Among 19,237 patients, 24.9% had no observed post-discharge therapy, 42.8% received metformin, 22.9% received insulin, and 9.4% received GLP-1RA/SGLT2i therapy. All active therapies were associated with lower mortality compared with no observed therapy, including GLP-1RA/SGLT2i (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.58-0.87), metformin (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.55-0.66), and insulin (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.67-0.84). Among active therapies, metformin was associated with lower mortality than insulin (HR, 0.61 [0.54-0.70]); GLP-1RA/SGLT2i comparisons with metformin and insulin were less precise. Metformin was also associated with lower cumulative incidence of heart failure hospitalization than no observed therapy and insulin, and lower stroke incidence than insulin. CONCLUSIONS: Observed glucose-lowering therapy initiation after CABG was associated with lower mortality compared with no observed therapy across all active treatment groups. These findings highlight a potential care gap and suggest that proper initiation of diabetes therapy after CABG represents an important opportunity to improve long-term outcomes following surgical revascularization.

title: Atherosclerotic plaque healing: mechanisms and clinical relevance.
abstract: Atherosclerotic plaque healing is a dynamic biological mechanism that occurrs after plaque disruption and represents an endogenous reparative response within the atherosclerotic lesion. This process unfolds through three partially overlapping phases: endogenous thrombus lysis, granulation tissue formation, and re-endothelialization. Through the coordinated interaction of circulating cells, vascular wall components, and soluble mediators, plaque healing promotes fibrous repair and structural stabilization of the disrupted plaque. For many years, plaque healing remained primarily a histopathological observation described in post-mortem studies. The advent of high-resolution intracoronary imaging, particularly optical coherence tomography, has enabled in vivo visualization of the characteristic layered morphology of healed plaques, providing direct clinical confirmation of these early pathological findings. These observations have significantly improved our understanding of the clinical significance of plaque healing. Healed plaques are more frequently observed in patients with chronic coronary syndromes, supporting the concept that healing contributes to plaque stabilization. At the same time, recurrent cycles of plaque disruption followed by repair may lead to progressive luminal narrowing, thereby contributing to the long-term progression of coronary atherosclerosis. This review provided an updated overview of the clinical significance and implications of healed plaques in coronary artery disease, the mechanisms underlying plaque healing, and examines emerging intracoronary and non-invasive imaging modalities that allow their in vivo identification.

title: Low-Voltage Area Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: The COAST-AF Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) for persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) has demonstrated modest success rates. Ablation of atrial low-voltage areas (LVA) has shown potential results, but more data are required. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether PVI plus LVA ablation is superior to PVI alone in reducing atrial arrhythmia recurrence in patients with AF. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Single-blind randomized clinical trial in 14 AF ablation centers in Canada. Adults with persistent AF of more than 3 months were enrolled between August 2018 and September 2024 and followed up for 18 to 36 months through April 2026. INTERVENTION: Patients were randomized to PVI plus LVA ablation or PVI alone. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was atrial arrhythmia recurrence beyond 90 days after a single catheter ablation procedure. Secondary outcomes included repeat ablation for AF, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia, emergency visits or hospitalization, arrhythmia recurrence over 18 months, procedure duration, total ablation delivery time, AF burden, and safety outcomes. The primary efficacy analysis was based on the modified intention-to-treat principle for patients who received the intervention. RESULTS: Among 508 enrolled patients, 253 were randomized to PVI plus LVA ablation and 255 to PVI alone. Mean (SD) age was 65.2 (9.0) years, 386 (76%) were male and 268 (54%) had LVA. After a mean (SD) follow-up of 21 (15) months, 124 (49.4%) randomized to PVI plus LVA and 146 (57.5%) randomized to PVI reached the primary outcome (hazard ratio [HR], 0.82; 95% CI, 0.65-1.04; P = .11). In the prespecified principal subgroup analysis of 268 patients with LVA, arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 68 of 138 patients (49.3%) following PVI plus LVA ablation compared with 90 of 130 patients (69.2%) following PVI alone (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.66-0.91; P = .002). Arrhythmia recurrence over 18 months (37.0% vs 56.2%; HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.64-0.92) and AF burden were lower after PVI plus LVA ablation in this group. Among patients without LVA, recurrence was similar between ablation groups (56 of 113 [49.6%] vs 51 of 113 [45.1%]; HR, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.90-1.32). Procedure duration and ablation delivery time were longer in the PVI plus LVA ablation group. Safety outcomes were similar between groups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, among patients with persistent AF, adjunctive LVA ablation did not significantly reduce atrial arrhythmia recurrence in the overall population over a mean 21-month follow-up. A prespecified principal subgroup analysis of patients with LVA suggested that adjunctive LVA ablation was consistent with reduced recurrence of atrial arrhythmias in this group. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, Identifier: NCT03347227.

title: Prognostic value of Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio after percutaneous coronary intervention.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) physiological indices have prognostic relevance. Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (μQFR) enables wire-free, rapid, single-view functional assessment, yet its long-term prognostic value after PCI remains incompletely established. AIMS: We sought to evaluate the prognostic value of post-PCI μQFR for long-term adverse outcomes. METHODS: This prespecified subgroup analysis of the FAVOR III China trial included 3,825 patients. All PCI-treated vessels with a reference diameter ≥2.5 mm and 50-90% diameter stenosis were analysed for offline post-PCI μQFR. The primary endpoint was 5-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; including death from any cause, myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven revascularisation). RESULTS: Post-PCI μQFR was successfully analysed in 4,196 vessels from 3,455 patients, with similar distributions between the randomised treatment groups. At 5 years, a low post-PCI μQFR was associated with a higher incidence of MACE compared with the intermediate and high post-PCI μQFR tertiles (23.1% vs 19.0% vs 17.2%; p=0.001). Using the highest tertile (μQFR>0.95) as a reference, adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) were 1.08 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.87-1.34) for the intermediate tertile (0.92-0.95) and 1.30 (95% CI: 1.06-1.60) for the lowest tertile (μQFR ≤0.91). Using a receiver operating characteristic-derived cutoff, MACE occurred more frequently in patients with post-PCI μQFR <0.94 (22.3% vs 17.4%, aHR 1.23, 95% CI: 1.04-1.47; p=0.02) than in those with post-PCI μQFR ≥0.94. No significant interaction was observed between treatment strategy and post-PCI μQFR (p for interaction=0.23). CONCLUSIONS: Post-PCI μQFR distributions were similar between treatment groups, but lower values were associated with higher 5-year adverse event risk without significant treatment interaction. Its limited binary discrimination supports use as a continuous metric for post-PCI physiological risk stratification. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT03656848).

title: Controversy: Anticoagulants need to be maintained after catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation in patients at risk of stroke-Pro and Contra.
abstract: The pillars of atrial fibrillation (AF) management include stroke prevention, patient-centred symptom directed decisions on rhythm or rate control, and the proactive management of comorbidities and lifestyle changes. These pillars are not in isolation; they are complementary to each other. While oral anticoagulants (OACs) are highly effective for reducing stroke and all-cause mortality in patients with AF, these drugs confer a risk of major bleeding, including intracranial bleeding. Evidence from clinical trials and observational data shows that early rhythm control, especially with catheter ablation, results in a reduction in stroke risk and/or the reduction in AF burden. The question arises therefore, whether in patients with intermediate or low stroke risk after successful catheter ablation, whether or not to continue or discontinue OAC. Recent randomized trials and observational data have created some debate about whether OAC can be routinely stopped after a successful catheter ablation procedure, without a higher risk of thromboembolism. In this pro/contra article, we will debate the arguments for and against the cessation of anti-coagulation after catheter ablation, in the context of recent evidence from clinical trials, observational data, and meta-analysis.

title: Statin-Ezetimibe Combination Therapy versus Statin Monotherapy in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: A Prespecified Secondary Analysis of the Randomized Ez-PAVE Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In a target-directed low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C)-lowering strategy, the impact of the initial treatment regimen has not been investigated in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. We compared the efficacy and safety of initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy versus statin monotherapy within intensive or conventional LDL-C-targeting strategies. METHODS: In this prespecified second randomization of the randomized Ez-PAVE trial (Effects of Ezetimibe Combination Therapy for Patients With Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: Randomized Comparison of LDL Cholesterol Targeting <70 versus <55 mg/dL) conducted at 17 centers in South Korea, a total of 3048 patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were enrolled between January 2021 and July 2022. Following the first randomization to either an intensive (<55 mg/dL) or conventional (<70 mg/dL) LDL-C-targeting strategy, patients underwent subsequent randomization (initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy [n=1525] versus statin monotherapy [n=1523]) and were followed up for 3 years. Lipid-lowering therapy was adjusted according to a predefined protocol to achieve LDL-C targets. The primary end point was a 3-year composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, any revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina. RESULTS: The mean±SD age was 64.4±9.0 years, and 638 patients (20.9%) were female. The incidence of the primary end point did not differ between statin-ezetimibe combination therapy (128 patients [8.5%]) and statin monotherapy (119 patients [7.9%]; hazard ratio, 1.07 [95% CI, 0.83-1.37]; P=0.596). Patients who received statin-ezetimibe combination therapy achieved lower median LDL-C levels during follow-up than those who received statin monotherapy in both the intensive-targeting (53 mg/dL [interquartile range, 45-62 mg/dL] versus 62 mg/dL [interquartile range, 53-74 mg/dL]) and conventional-targeting (63 mg/dL [interquartile range, 55-73 mg/dL] versus 70 mg/dL [interquartile range, 62-81 mg/dL]) strategies. During follow-up, ezetimibe was added to the treatment regimen of 241 patients (34.3%) and 177 patients (24.8%) who initially received statin monotherapy in the intensive- and conventional-targeting strategies, respectively. The treatment effect of intensive-targeting versus conventional-targeting strategies was consistent regardless of therapy regimens without significant heterogeneity (Pinteraction=0.583). The safety end points were similar between the groups. CONCLUSIONS: Within a target-directed LDL-C-lowering strategy, cardiovascular efficacy and safety did not differ significantly, whether initiated as statin-ezetimibe combination therapy or as statin monotherapy, but combination therapy facilitated achievement of a lower LDL-C target. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04626973.

title: Role of reverse remodelling in recurrence of atrial fibrillation after patient-tailored catheter ablation.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Catheter ablation (CA) is a curative treatment for atrial fibrillation (AF), yet success rates remain sub-optimal, with ∼50% of patients with persistent AF experiencing recurrence after 1 year. This may be due to the self-perpetuating nature of AF, which remodels atrial structure and cellular properties, while successful treatment can induce reverse remodelling (RR). This study develops a patient-specific CA strategy to directly target re-entrant drivers (RDs) and investigates the role of RR in AF recurrence. METHODS: Left atrial (LA) models were reconstructed from LGE-MRI scans of AF patients (n = 15) and coupled with the Courtemanche-Ramirez-Nattel (CRN) electrophysiology model. RDs were induced via pacing, identified using DGM analysis, and targeted ablation was performed in-silico. Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) was applied as a reference. Following termination, AF recurrence was tested under three levels of electrical reverse remodelling (ERR: 0%, 50%, and 100%), with and without structural reverse remodelling (SRR). RESULTS: Targeted ablation acutely terminated AF in all patient-specific models. After the first procedure, AF recurrence decreased progressively from 55% at 0% ERR to 36.7% at 50% ERR and 5% at 100% ERR; with additional SRR, recurrence was further reduced to 46.7%, 26.7%, and 0%, respectively. After the second CA procedure, AF recurrence rate was 42.9%, 17.9%, and 0% without SRR and 25%, 14.3%, and 0% with SRR. CONCLUSION: This study highlights the importance of RR for therapy success, with a novel targeted CA technique ensuring <5% AF recurrence in patient-specific simulations. After clinical validation, this approach can help improve long-term patient outcomes.

title: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Sudden Cardiac Death: Epidemiology, Mechanisms, Risk Stratification, and Prevention.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as the most prevalent chronic metabolic liver disease worldwide. Cardiovascular adverse events have long been the leading cause of death in the MASLD population, far exceeding liver-related mortality. Sudden cardiac death (SCD) represents the most insidious and rapidly progressing extreme clinical phenotype among these cardiovascular complications. However, the relationship between MASLD and SCD has long received insufficient attention. Accumulating evidence from clinical studies indicates that MASLD is associated with elevated sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) risk independent of conventional cardiometabolic risk factors. Notably, while non-invasive clinical proxies of hepatic steatosis (such as the fatty liver index) identify individuals with heightened susceptibility to SCA, advancing liver fibrosis shows the strongest, gradient-dependent association with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, although its relation to SCA or SCD specifically requires confirmation. Sudden death in MASLD may result from primary ventricular arrhythmias or, in advanced cirrhosis, from non-shockable arrest due to hemodynamic, infectious, or metabolic decompensation. Although shared cardiometabolic risk factors account for a substantial portion of this association, proposed mechanisms include insulin resistance-related myocardial energy disturbances, inflammation-associated myocardial and electrophysiological remodeling, cirrhosis-associated circulatory dysfunction, and gut-derived endotoxemia. In clinical practice, non-invasive fibrosis scores, circulating biomarkers, and imaging parameters represent promising candidate risk markers for evaluating electrophysiological vulnerability, though a validated, MASLD-specific SCD risk prediction model remains to be established. Strategies such as lifestyle intervention, metabolic-targeted pharmacotherapy, and intensive management of cardiovascular risk factors may interrupt the progression from MASLD to SCD. This review summarizes the current evidence to inform cardiovascular risk management across the course of MASLD.

title: Plozasiran for Severe Hypertriglyceridemia and Risk of Pancreatitis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe hypertriglyceridemia is associated with an increased risk of acute pancreatitis. Plozasiran, a small interfering RNA targeting APOC3 messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis. METHODS: In two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. These trials had identical designs, end points, and analytic plans. The primary end point was the percent change in the fasting plasma triglyceride level from baseline to month 12. Key secondary end points were the percent change in the fasting triglyceride level from baseline to month 10, a fasting triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter) and less than 150 mg per deciliter (1.7 mmol per liter), the percent change in the fasting serum triglyceride level at month 12 for patients with a baseline triglyceride level of 880 mg per deciliter or greater, and changes in remnant cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol. A pooled analysis addressed adjudicated acute pancreatitis, incidence, and first-event timing. RESULTS: At month 12, patients in the plozasiran groups had a median triglyceride level that was lower than the baseline level by 79% and 81% in the two trials. These reductions corresponded to a median difference in the plozasiran groups as compared with the placebo groups (placebo-adjusted change) of -45 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -51 to -38) and -47 percentage points (95% CI, -54 to -39). A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (P<0.001). The rates of acute pancreatitis were 1 per 100 patient-years with plozasiran and 5 per 100 patient-years with placebo (rate ratio, 0.22; P = 0.008). Adverse events during treatment occurred in 73% of the patients in both the pooled plozasiran and placebo groups. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. (Funded by Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals; SHASTA-3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06347003; SHASTA-4, NCT06347016.).

title: Prediction of coronary events by computed tomography-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (CT-μFR) provides a non-invasive measure of vessel-level ischaemia but may not capture local haemodynamic abnormalities reflected by the longitudinal pressure gradient across the lesion (CT-μFR gradient). AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the association of CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient with 3-year vessel-level subsequent coronary events and to determine the incremental prognostic value of their combined assessment. METHODS: Our study included a total of 885 vessels from 312 patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or stable angina and had prior CCTA performed 6 months to 3 years earlier. CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient were assessed by an independent core laboratory blinded to the clinical data. The primary outcome was 3-year subsequent coronary events (a composite of vessel-specific myocardial infarction or urgent revascularisation for ACS). The discrimination ability of predictive models was assessed using Harrell's C-index. RESULTS: Vessels with CT-μFR ≤0.80 or a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm had a higher risk of events than those with CT-μFR>0.80 (79.1% vs 20.4%, adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.26-8.96; p<0.001) or a CT-μFR gradient <0.004/mm (72.6% vs 27.4%, adjusted HR 4.08, 95% CI: 3.15-5.28; p<0.001), respectively. Among vessels with CT-μFR>0.80, a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm remained associated with increased risk (adjusted HR 2.59, 95% CI: 1.63-4.11; p<0.001). Adding the CT-μFR gradient to CT-μFR improved discrimination in the overall cohort (C-index 0.700 to 0.755; p<0.001) as well as the subgroup with CT-μFR>0.80 (C-index 0.575 to 0.655; p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Both CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient are independently associated with 3-year subsequent coronary events. Their combined assessment improves risk stratification beyond CT-μFR alone. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04794868).

title: Coronary angiography in heart transplants from donors older than 40: a Eurotransplant study.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The increasing age of heart donors in Europe raises concerns about undetected coronary artery disease (CAD), a contributor to early graft dysfunction and long-term complications. This study examined the association between donor coronary angiography (CA) and heart transplant utilization, particularly in donors aged >40 years. METHODS: A total of 20 681 donor heart offers reported to Eurotransplant between 2004 and 2020 were analysed. The use of CA, donor characteristics, and acceptance rates were assessed. CAD status was imputed for donors without angiography using logistic regression based on clinical risk factors. Transplantation probabilities were modelled using observed and imputed CAD severity to explore potential differences under a scenario of broader CA availability. RESULTS: CA was performed in 23.5% of cases, predominantly in older donors and those with cardiovascular risk factors. Among donors with CA, 37.5% had CAD, which was significantly associated with age, male sex, hypertension, and smoking. Donors with normal CA findings had lower odds of rejection compared with those without CA (odds ratio 0.36, P < .0001). In a counterfactual model, broader CA availability in donors aged >40 years was associated with a higher estimated transplant utilization (56.4%-67.1%), corresponding to a model-based increase of ∼535 transplants. CONCLUSIONS: In this observational cohort, CA availability was associated with differences in donor heart utilization, particularly when findings were normal or showed non-significant CAD. These findings suggest that angiographic information may reduce diagnostic uncertainty and support clinical decision-making in older donors. A risk-adapted, resource-sensitive approach to CA use is warranted.
